executive_summary.company_overview: Kaltefluss GmbH is a Munich-based seed-stage deep-tech hardware startup developing high-temperature industrial heat pumps (up to 200°C) using a proprietary turbo-compressor architecture with natural refrigerants. The company targets food processing and chemical plants in the DACH region, with two pilot installations operating near Augsburg at TRL 5-6.
executive_summary.strongest_themes: Industrial decarbonisation and process heat electrification are among the highest-priority themes in EU and German funding landscapes right now. Kaltefluss's core product — replacing gas-fired process heat with electrified high-temperature heat — maps directly onto EIC Accelerator deep-tech mandates, EU Innovation Fund industrial decarbonisation priorities, Horizon Europe CL5 process heat topics, and German federal programmes. The 200°C capability and natural refrigerant differentiation strengthen the 'breakthrough technology' narrative required by EIC and Horizon.
executive_summary.strongest_geographies: Germany and the EU are the optimal funding geographies. German federal programmes (BAFA, DBU, BMWK) provide accessible near-term non-dilutive capital, while EU-level programmes (EIC Accelerator, Innovation Fund, Horizon Europe) offer transformational funding amounts and investor-signalling value. No UK or non-EU funding landscape is relevant given the company's operational footprint.
executive_summary.key_constraints: TRL 5-6 is borderline for some deployment-focused programmes (EU Innovation Fund typically prefers TRL 6+). The company's very low public profile and pre-revenue status may weaken EIC and Innovation Fund applications that reward commercial traction. Horizon Europe requires multi-country consortia, adding coordination burden. BAFA and BMWK programmes primarily fund end-users rather than technology developers, limiting direct access.

strategic_recommendations.best_fit_strategy: Pursue a two-track strategy: (1) apply immediately to DBU Green Start-up for accessible near-term non-dilutive capital while building public profile, and (2) prepare a high-quality EIC Accelerator application (Open or Challenge track) as the primary transformational funding target. Use the two Augsburg pilot installations as the cornerstone of all application narratives — they are the company's strongest evidence of technical validation and commercial relevance.
strategic_recommendations.best_geographies: Germany (DBU, BAFA demand-side pull, BMWK) and EU-wide (EIC Accelerator, EU Innovation Fund, Horizon Europe CL5). Germany provides the most accessible near-term routes; EU-level programmes offer the largest funding amounts and greatest strategic leverage.
strategic_recommendations.strongest_pathways: Priority 1: DBU Green Start-up (open now, direct, low burden, €125k). Priority 2: EIC Accelerator Challenge — Deep Tech for Climate Adaptation 2026 (named challenge, highest thematic alignment). Priority 3: EIC Accelerator Open (parallel or sequential track). Priority 4: EU Innovation Fund Small-Scale (prepare now, apply when next window opens). Priority 5: Horizon Europe CL5 (build consortium now for 2025-2026 calls).
strategic_recommendations.key_partnerships: To unlock Horizon Europe CL5 funding, Kaltefluss needs consortium partners: a German or European research institute (e.g. Fraunhofer IEG, RWTH Aachen, TU Munich) and at least one industrial end-user (food processing or chemical company). For BAFA demand-side pull, formalising relationships with the two Augsburg pilot customers is critical. A Fraunhofer partnership would also strengthen EIC and Innovation Fund applications.
strategic_recommendations.capability_gaps: The company needs to build public profile urgently — no Crunchbase, LinkedIn, or press coverage weakens EIC and Innovation Fund applications. A published technical validation report or peer-reviewed paper from the Augsburg pilots would significantly strengthen TRL claims. Commercial letters of intent or early revenue from pilot customers would materially improve EIC Accelerator scoring.
strategic_recommendations.key_risks: EIC Accelerator has a ~5% success rate and requires significant preparation investment. The Innovation Fund's TRL requirements may exclude Kaltefluss until TRL 6 is more firmly demonstrated. German political uncertainty around industrial decarbonisation funding (BMWK budget pressures) could affect programme continuity. Consortium assembly for Horizon Europe is time-consuming and uncertain.

company_profile.name: Kaltefluss GmbH
company_profile.classification: Deep Tech / Climate Tech / Industrial Hardware
company_profile.value_proposition: Kaltefluss builds high-temperature industrial heat pumps (up to 200°C output) that replace gas-fired process heat for food processing and chemical plants, enabling industrial decarbonisation in the DACH region.
company_profile.technology: Proprietary turbo-compressor architecture using natural refrigerants, capable of delivering process heat up to 200°C — a technically differentiated approach versus conventional reciprocating or scroll compressor heat pumps that typically top out below 120°C.
company_profile.primary_outcome: Industrial decarbonisation — each installed unit displaces approximately 1,200 tonnes of CO2 per year by replacing gas-fired process heat.
secondary_benefits: Reduction in industrial energy costs for end-users as gas prices remain elevated
Supports DACH industrial sector compliance with EU decarbonisation and energy efficiency regulations
Enables food processing and chemical plants to decarbonise without full process redesign
company_profile.trl: TRL 5-6 — proprietary turbo-compressor technology validated in relevant environment; two pilot installations operating at customer sites near Augsburg, but no serial production or commercial deployment achieved yet.
company_profile.website_summary: Kaltefluss GmbH is a Munich-based deep-tech hardware startup developing high-temperature industrial heat pumps that deliver process heat up to 200°C using a proprietary turbo-compressor and natural refrigerants. Its systems are designed to replace gas-fired boilers in energy-intensive industries such as food processing and chemicals. The company is at pilot stage with two installations running at customer sites near Augsburg, Germany.
company_profile.external_findings: No independent press coverage, Crunchbase listing, or LinkedIn profile for Kaltefluss GmbH was found in external searches, suggesting the company has a very low public profile consistent with an early-stage seed startup. Broader market context confirms strong European demand for high-temperature industrial heat pumps using natural refrigerants, with the AHEAD project and others validating technical feasibility of fossil-free steam generation at comparable temperature ranges. No evidence of UK presence, UK customers, or UK-registered entities was found.
